correctness.rationale: The geometric-Poisson-Lindley PGF yields an exact two-component geometric/negative-binomial mixture and a closed innovation survival. Exact rational factorization of 1-U establishes the full admissibility boundary, including U=1 at equality. A constructive coupling proves strict first-order monotonicity. Direct multiplication of the first two transition columns gives the adjacent determinant; a finite all-positive-coefficient polynomial proves the initial sign for every positive parameter, while a strictly positive derivative gives a unique real crossing on the interior, an endpoint exception, and a sharp critical divergence law. The embedded independent-path checker successfully verified the finite identities and exact-rational witness; infinite quantifiers follow from the displayed proof.

value.rationale: For an established stationary count-series model with explicit transitions, the result identifies a previously unclassified sharp difference between stochastic monotonicity and local likelihood-ratio ordering; on the whole interior, negative adjacent minors rule out strong TP2 methods, while the endpoint remains positive for the same minor family. The unique crossing and its reciprocal-distance divergence provide practical interpretability for finite observed state ranges close to the admissibility boundary. This is a structural classification, not a routine substitution or an arbitrary finite table cell.
